label: WardStock - Full Sync
info:
Aug 2026 (Ward: "make a flow that does the steps to sync HA and GoDaddy and then exports all the data into the share directory"). Orchestrates the three existing flows in sequence, without duplicating any of their logic, via Node-RED's core Link Call / Link In / Link Out nodes — this flow calls into the SAME entry point each flow's own inject trigger already uses, so running a step from here behaves identically to running that flow by hand.

All three Link Call nodes use DYNAMIC targeting (msg.target set to the target Link In node's NAME immediately before each call — see n_fs_check_import_branch, n_fs_after_step1, n_fs_after_step2), not static id references. First attempt used static (links: [id]) and broke on the very first real run — 'target link-in node '' not found' — because importing these files as separate pieces let Node-RED renumber a node id that a DIFFERENT file's static reference had hardcoded; dynamic-by-name survives that since names aren't touched by id renumbering. This only works because each of the three Link In node names below is now globally unique across the whole instance (GoDaddy Restore from File / GoDaddy Pull / wherewhen Data Export, each suffixed '(Full Sync entry)') — Node-RED's dynamic resolution matches by name and silently uses the first match if a name isn't unique, so don't rename a Link In node without checking nothing else still expects the old name, and don't reuse the same name across two Link In nodes anywhere in the instance.

  1. GoDaddy Restore (from file) — godaddy_restore_from_file_flow.json, via n_fs_call_restore, dynamic
     target 'GoDaddy Restore from File (Full Sync entry)'. Conditional: n_fs_check_import_exec checks
     whether /share/wardstock_restore_import.json actually exists before calling in, so an ordinary night
     with nothing staged is a true no-op (not a timeout/error). That flow's own success path now
     archives the file afterward (n_grf_archive_prep/exec, added alongside this flow) so a processed
     import is never re-uploaded on the next run.
  2. GoDaddy Pull — godaddy_pull_flow.json, via n_fs_call_pull, dynamic target 'GoDaddy Pull (Full Sync
     entry)'. Reconciles GoDaddy into InfluxDB/local archive — same request this flow's own 15-minute
     schedule makes.
  3. wherewhen Data Export — wherewhen_data_export_flow.json, via n_fs_call_export, dynamic target
     'wherewhen Data Export (Full Sync entry)'. Dumps everything InfluxDB holds to a fresh timestamped
     /share/wardstock_data_backup/<stamp>/ folder,
     then that flow's own new retention pass prunes old ones (see its tab info for the GFS policy: last
     7 days kept in full, then weekly through 30 days, then monthly forever).

Each step's own success/failure is logged independently under its OWN job_name in sync_job_runs
(godaddy_restore_from_file / godaddy_pull / wherewhen_export), exactly as if it had been triggered
directly — this flow does not change or duplicate that. On top of that, THIS flow logs its own
job_name=full_sync entry summarizing the whole run (which steps ran, which failed, if any).

Steps run in sequence regardless of a prior step's outcome (a failed restore or pull shouldn't block
the export — each downstream step is independently useful/safe to attempt), but any failure is
collected into msg.full_sync_failures and reported in the final status (status=failed if anything
failed, rather than silently reporting success).

Triggers: manual (n_fs_trigger_manual) plus nightly at 2am (n_fs_trigger_nightly) — the nightly
schedule is what actually makes the backup retention policy meaningful (it needs a regular cadence
to prune against). wherewhen_data_export_flow.json's own standalone 'Weekly - Sunday 3am' trigger was
redundant against this nightly run and Ward confirmed disabling it (Aug 23 2026) — see that flow's
tab info; it's disabled (d:true), not deleted, so it can be re-enabled if Full Sync is ever turned off.

No separate companion test flow (same reasoning godaddy_restore_from_file_flow.json gives for not
having one): every step here calls flows that are already exercised on their own, so the only
genuinely new logic is the sequencing, the import-file existence check, and the failure aggregation —
small enough that this tab's own info and node.warn output cover what a dedicated test flow would.

UNTESTED — same caveat as every new flow in this project, compounded here by depending on Link
Call/Link In/Link Out (never used elsewhere in this project before now) working as documented in
your actual Node-RED version. Verify a manual run end-to-end before trusting the nightly schedule.
